questions.q: What problem does a Record Type solve, per this lesson?
options: It lets a single object present different picklist values, page layouts, and business processes depending on which Record Type a record is assigned
It lets a company delete objects it doesn't need
It converts a custom object into a standard object
It merges two separate objects into one automatically
questions.explain: Record Types let one object, like Opportunity, support genuinely different business processes without forcing them into one compromised picklist.

questions.q: In the lesson's example, what's different between a 'New Business' and a 'Renewal' Opportunity Record Type?
options: They show different Stage picklist values, even though both are Opportunity records with a Stage field
They are stored in two completely separate objects
One has a Stage field and the other does not
There is no real difference between them
questions.explain: Both are Opportunity records with a Stage field, but the available Stage values differ depending on the assigned Record Type.

questions.q: What risk does the lesson warn about when reporting on Opportunity Stage without checking Record Type?
options: Quietly mixing two unrelated business processes together, or filtering for a Stage value that only exists for one Record Type and missing the rest
The report will always fail to run
Record Type has no effect on any report
Opportunity Stage cannot be reported on at all if Record Types exist
questions.explain: A Stage filter written without Record Type awareness can misleadingly mix processes or silently exclude an entire Record Type's records.

questions.q: Is the Record Type field itself available for use in reports, per this lesson?
options: Yes — it's available on the record and in reports, so an analyst can check it directly
No — Record Type is invisible and cannot be reported on
Only Salesforce administrators can see the Record Type field
Record Type only exists on custom objects, never standard ones
questions.explain: The lesson states the fix is straightforward because the Record Type field itself is available on the record and in reports.

questions.q: What would happen to New Business Opportunity records if a report filtered strictly for Stage = 'Renewal Review'?
options: They would be excluded, since 'Renewal Review' is a Stage value that only exists for the Renewal Record Type
They would all be included automatically regardless of Stage
The report would throw an error and fail to run
New Business records would be converted to Renewal records
questions.explain: Since 'Renewal Review' isn't a valid Stage value for New Business records, filtering on it would silently miss every New Business Opportunity.
